| 2026-09-09 | 🔴 **A LOG LINE THAT CANNOT REPORT FAILURE UNDER ANY CONDITION — and the seat proved it by registering a tenant whose DATABASE DOES NOT EXIST.** The gate said `migrated++` counts tenants whose migrations failed. **It counts a tenant whose database is absent entirely:** registered against `tenant_does_not_exist`, **proved absent in `pg_database` and present in the loop's own query**, booted, and got *"Tenant DB migrations complete {migrated:8, skipped:0, total:8}"*. 🔑 **MECHANISM NAMED TO THE LINE, twice over: `migrateDatabase` swallows every per-statement error in its own inner try/catch and returns `applied`, so it NEVER THROWS, so the loop's catch arm is DEAD CODE — and `new pg.Pool()` does not connect eagerly, so a total connection failure surfaces inside `pool.query` and is swallowed there too.** ⚠ **AND THE THIRD LEG, found while building the instrument rather than while looking for it: the product hard-codes `?sslmode=require` and `pg-connection-string` 2.12.0 treats `require` as VERIFY-FULL** — proven both ways before it was trusted (no CA → *"unable to verify the first certificate"*; with a locally-signed CA → connected). **Consequence: on any deployment whose tenant DB does not present a CA-verifiable cert, the tenant loop connects to NOTHING and the counter reports `migrated:N` anyway.** **WEDNESDAY'S RULING: all three legs go on KS-1055 as ONE logical path** — *tenant provisioning is broken and nothing reports it* — deny-all on arrival · cannot connect without a trusted CA · a counter that reports success under every failure. **Three tickets would each look survivable alone; together they are an outage nobody would ever see.** 🔑 **THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: a defect found while BUILDING THE INSTRUMENT is not incidental — the seat had to defeat VERIFY-FULL to measure anything, which means every real deployment meets the same wall, and the thing that stopped the measurement IS the finding.** | finding | +1 (a success-reporting counter disproved by an action rather than by reading — a tenant with no database at all) · +1 (NEW: a defect discovered while building the instrument, where the obstacle to measurement IS the production failure mode) | [[2026-08-07_a-check-that-cannot-fail]] (**a log line whose failure branch is unreachable by construction**) · [[2026-08-06_artifact-presence-is-not-execution]] · [[2026-09-08_a-false-absence-is-usually-my-own-instrument]] (rule 8: ask whether the answer is POSSIBLE) · [[2026-08-06_never-discard-stderr]] (**swallowed in an inner try/catch — the same rule, in someone else's code**) | **Fix commissioned as the ride-along, measurement banked. **a well-formatted output is exactly where that assumption breaks.** **RULE: a red-proof matrix asserts its GREEN cells mechanically — `[ "$rc_green" -eq 0 ] || { echo "BASELINE FAILED"; exit 1; }` — because the human formatting the table is the one least likely to read it.** | correction | +1 (check-the-refusal-before-the-kill — chained by the coordinator who quoted the rule to three seats the same night) · +1 (all-fail signature printed on screen and not read;
